result.title: Workplace Scheduling: Bring Forward and Put Off
result.objective: Learners will understand and use bring forward and put off to describe moving work events earlier or later.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s1, what does bring forward mean?

options.text: To move the equipment check to an earlier day.
options.explanation: It is correct because the coordinator moved the check earlier since Friday is booked.

options.text: To delay the equipment check to a later day.
options.explanation: It is wrong because delaying means moving later, the opposite of the context.

options.text: To cancel the equipment check completely.
options.explanation: It is wrong because the check still happens, only the date changes.

exercises.explanation: The context shows the check happens one day earlier, not later or cancelled.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses bring forward correctly and naturally.

options.text: The team decided to bring forward the workshop to Thursday to avoid the Friday booking.
options.explanation: It is correct because it uses bring forward with correct grammar to mean moving to an earlier date.

options.text: She bring forward the presentation to Monday because the client is available.
options.explanation: It is wrong because She bring should be She brings to agree with the subject.

options.text: We will bring forward the review on next Tuesday to finish earlier.
options.explanation: It is wrong because on next Tuesday should be next Tuesday without on.

exercises.explanation: Only one option uses bring forward with correct grammar to mean an earlier time.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s3, what does put off mean?

options.text: To start the walkthrough earlier than planned.
options.explanation: It is wrong because starting earlier is the opposite of delaying until more volunteers are available.

options.text: To postpone the walkthrough to a later time.
options.explanation: It is correct because the team delays the walkthrough until more volunteers are available.
It is wrong because the walkthrough may still happen later, not be cancelled forever.

exercises.explanation: The context shows a delay until more volunteers are available, not an earlier start or cancellation.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses put off correctly and naturally.

options.text: We had to put off the site visit until next week when more staff are available.
options.explanation: It is correct because it uses put off with correct grammar to mean postponing to a later time.

options.text: They has put off the training until June due to scheduling issues.
options.explanation: It is wrong because They has should be They have to agree with the plural subject.

options.text: He decided to put off the meeting in Monday morning because of the delay.
options.explanation: It is wrong because in Monday morning should be on Monday morning for days.

exercises.explanation: Only one option uses put off with correct grammar to mean postponing.

exercises.prompt: Imagine you are an office assistant emailing a client about a product meeting. Write 2-3 sentences explaining you need to postpone the meeting and suggesting a new arrangement. Use the phrase put off.
exercises.sampleAnswer: I am writing to let you know we need to put off our product meeting until next Tuesday. More team members will be available then to discuss the details with you.
selfCheck: I wrote 2-3 sentences as a message with a new role and purpose.
I used put off correctly to mean postponing to a later time.
My message suggests a new arrangement for the meeting.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
